belief: People see my difference before they see me.
origins: First impressions are fast and often shaped by what is visible. Repeated experiences of being pigeonholed lead us to expect it always.
teaches: God said to Samuel, “Man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” Jesus saw people as individuals: Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was called by name and asked, “What do you want Me to do for you?” (Mark 10:51). “Stop judging by outward appearances, and start judging justly” (John 7:24). Some people will notice first and then look deeper. Others will meet you directly, and over time, those who matter see the whole you.
self_statements: I will always be defined by it.
They never see the real me.
errors: Believing people see only my difference or only me.
Predicting that people will never look deeper.
Feeling noticed and concluding I am defined.
questions: Who has looked past my difference?
What do I want people to know first?
What does it feel like when someone sees me fully?
What conversation starters let people see more of me?
truth: God sees my heart, and many people will, too. I can guide first impressions by sharing what matters about me, and I can seek those who look deeper.
hw_truths: I can lead with who I am.
I am more than my difference.
log: Each week, note one person who saw more than your difference.
actions: Share an interest or strength early.
prayer: Lord, people notice my difference first. Thank You that You see my heart. Give me friends who see all of me. Amen.
